rows.question: does the estate know what hardware a host contains, class by class — and does it admit which classes nobody looked at?

probes.observed: every class the review named is reported for this host: cpu=PRESENT, memory=PRESENT, motherboard=PRESENT, bios=PRESENT, firmware=PRESENT, pci=PRESENT, gpu=PRESENT, nic=PRESENT, storage_controller=ABSENT, disk=PRESENT, raid=PRESENT, tpm=PRESENT, hsm=PRESENT, smart_card=PRESENT, crypto_accelerator=ABSENT
processor Intel(R) Xeon(R) Gold 6430 from lscpu, 2 memory module(s) from dmidecode -t memory
GPU 'ASPEED Graphics [2000]', RAID 'PERC H755 [10e2]' and NICs from the PCI class codes; a non-RAID storage controller is ABSENT (the bus answered) rather than UNKNOWN
2 firmware revision(s) recorded against the component that carries each one
with lspci unavailable the GPU, RAID and storage classes are UNKNOWN and name the reason — not ABSENT, which would have read as 'this server has no GPU'

with the reader stripped the TPM is UNKNOWN and says nobody looked; with tpm2_getcap in the transcript it is PRESENT (IFX firmware 7.63.8.13139) — the third state is what keeps the first answer honest
1 reader(s) from opensc-tool with card_present=True; the two facts are separate because an empty reader and an absent reader are different findings

Windows fills CPU, memory modules, BIOS, motherboard, disk and TPM from CIM, and the device tree now names PCI, GPU, NIC and storage controllers too — only RAID and a crypto accelerator stay UNKNOWN, because Windows exposes an array as a property of its controller and has no accelerator class at all
both UNKNOWN classes on Windows carry the reason the platform gives, and a Windows reader that did not read the device tree says so instead of reporting an empty bus
every component is derived from facts the readers already produced; the module owns no table, so a component cannot drift away from the observation behind it

rows.question: does an HSM carry the twelve facts a bank needs — and none of the five it must never carry?

probes.observed: 12/12 facts present on the observation: vendor, model, firmware, device identity, HA state, partitions, algorithms, key types, certificates, capabilities and PQC
5/5 refusals through the HSM scanner itself: private key, secret key, pin, wrapped key, plaintext
certificate dependencies arrive as references, so the twin draws them as edges only where a record names both ends
an application→HSM relationship is an evidenced edge in the usage graph, not a string on the observation: a text field could not carry the evidence id the twin needs
PQC capability is explicit: ['ML-DSA-65'] on firmware 8.2.1
the row reads the scanner's own observation (hsm, firmware 8.2.1), so guide 129 cannot drift from the HSM model in guide 128

rows.question: is 'this application uses this HSM' proven by a record that names both ends, or assumed because both exist?

probes.observed: 1 application(s) use HSM-01: Payment API (HIGH, EV-9b3c809b2a5f)
Statement Worker shares the estate with the appliance and shares no configuration with it, so no edge exists — coexistence is not a dependency
a config naming a token label no discovered appliance carries is reported UNRESOLVED, because a dependency on something the estate has not found is worth knowing
when two appliances carry the same token label the edge is refused as AMBIGUOUS with both candidates named; picking one would be a guess wearing an evidence id
4 SUPPORTS link(s) from the observation: RSA-3072 (RSA), ECDSA-P256 (ECDSA), AES-256 (AES), ML-DSA-65 (PQC)
the edge type itself refuses a construction with no evidence, so the graph cannot be filled by assertion even by a caller that skips the helpers
resolved=1, unresolved=1, ambiguous=0

rows.question: if this HSM fails, what breaks — and is the answer evidenced at every hop?

probes.observed: HSM-01 → 2 application(s) → 1 service(s) → 1 critical business system(s) (Card Authorization)
HSM-01 failure reaches 2 application(s); 1 service(s); 1 critical business system(s) (Card Authorization)
1 service hop(s), each with the evidence id of the application→hardware edge and of the service mapping
with no service record for the payment applications the answer names them as unmapped rather than reporting that a failure would reach nothing
the hop that reaches a business system needs its own record, so the business view cannot be asserted any more than the hardware edge can
the config-proven edge is HIGH and the CMDB service mapping is MEDIUM; the answer reports MEDIUM, because the chain is only as strong as its weakest citation
an appliance nothing proven depends on produces that sentence — not a reassuring zero that hides a missing collector

rows.question: is a hardware change first class — named, evidenced, versioned and correlated — or just a log line?

probes.observed: the bump produced ['FIRMWARE_CHANGED', 'CRYPTO_CAPABILITY_CHANGED', 'PQC_CAPABILITY_ADDED', 'HSM_CAPABILITY_CHANGED']
every change payload is firmware versions, algorithm names and evidence ids
4 drift row(s) became live events with evidence ids, through the same controller the estate runs
the PQC row is CORRELATED with the TLS profile switch and the certificate reissue (verdicts ['SUSPICIOUS', 'CORRELATED', 'CORRELATED', 'CORRELATED'])
the correlation carries its own disclaimer, so a change board cannot read a timestamp as proof
the feed holds 4 hardware change(s) for the 4 rows the diff produced — no double counting across the seam
the HBOM version moved 2 → 3 when the firmware did, and the two documents differ — the drift is a version in the twin, not a row in a log
the change names what the CBOM gains (ML-DSA-65) and what it loses (nothing), so a CBOM projection after the change has something to say

rows.question: do the collection guards actually refuse — under a hostile path, a moving file and an elevated process?

probes.observed: symlink=refused, hardlink=refused, special file=refused, oversized=refused, input mutation=refused — a symlink never reaches an open, a hard link is refused for aliasing, a FIFO is not a file, an oversized input stops at the limit and a file that changes mid-read is refused rather than half-read
private key=refused, secret text=refused — the PEM spelling ('BEGIN PRIVATE KEY') is refused as well as the underscore form, which it was not until this drill ran it

manifest tampering=refused, privilege=refused, expiry=refused, runtime promotion=refused, algorithm promotion=refused, policy promotion=refused — an elevated process is refused, an expired manifest is refused, a tampered manifest no longer matches its digest, a snapshot cannot claim whole-host coverage, a CMDB claim cannot be promoted past MEDIUM and an unknown evidence kind cannot be invented
the same code path reads a real file, so the refusals above are not a reader that refuses everything

3/3 non-allowlisted argument(s) refused (tpm2_getcap properties-variable, tpm2_getcap --tcti=device, opensc-tool --read-certificate) while the one shape each tool is run as still passes — a TPM subcommand or a card-certificate read is not reachable by asking the reader for it
forcing `security_qualification` to FAIL removed green from 1/1 area(s) that rested on it

reclassification.security: Security moves from 🔴 broad concern to 🟡 qualification still required: the collection guards refuse rather than assert, and what remains is qualification on a bank host and a Windows runner, not an open security hole.

limits: no bank hardware was touched: the Linux and Windows hosts are recorded facts, the HSM is a synthetic observation, and the application configurations are fixtures shaped like the real files
the component inventory grades what the readers can see, not what a machine has: a class nobody looked at is UNKNOWN, and UNKNOWN is not an absence
on Windows, PCI, GPU, RAID, storage-controller and NIC classes have no reader yet; that is a gap in the CIM allowlist and is reported as UNKNOWN rather than as a machine without those parts
smart cards and crypto accelerators are only as good as the reader that supplies them: this artifact projects a PC/SC or PCI record, it does not open a reader
the usage graph reads configuration files handed to it; nothing here watches a running process open a PKCS#11 session, so an application that uses the HSM without configuring it is invisible
a token label shared by two appliances is refused rather than resolved; on a real estate that refusal is a labelling job, not a bug
the business impact walk depends on service and business-system records a bank maintains; this artifact exercises the chain with CMDB-shaped fixtures and does not connect to a CMDB
drift here is a single-appliance diff executed in-process; it does not prove what a fleet does when a firmware rollback lands on one unit of a cluster
the security row executes the collection guards on this runner as an unprivileged or elevated process, whichever it is; Windows traversal guards need a Windows host

the Windows device tree is projected from `PNPClass`, a Setup Class name and not a PCI class code: a smart-card reader is a reader (whether a card is seated is a separate fact) and a controller Windows calls `SCSIAdapter` is recorded as a storage controller, not as the array behind it

on Linux the two new readers run as the same unprivileged user as `lspci`, so a host with a policy that denies `/dev/tpm0` or hides the PC/SC socket reports TPM and smart-card as UNKNOWN with that reason rather than as absent
